newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: POLL-Meralco 1st half net seen up 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Meralco 1st half net seen up 16 pct.

text.p: Manila Electric Co (Meralco), the Philippines' biggest power distributor, could post higher net income for the first half of 1997 despite slower sales growth, according to analysts.

A Reuters poll of seven brokerages completed on Tuesday showed that for the first six months, the utility would register an average 16.2 percent rise in net income to 2.84 billion pesos ($107.61 million) compared to 2.38 billion pesos a year ago.
"There will be growth in kilowatt-hour (kw/h) sales but it will be single-digit and that's what's sad and disappointing," said Noel Reyes, vice-president at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
Most analysts said they were initially looking at 11 percent kw/h sales growth for the full year but were now cutting it to between eight and nine percent.
Guoco Securities, ING Barings, Philippine Asia Equity and Anscor Hagedorn said their full-year net income forecasts would be changed in the next few days to reflect the lower sales growth.
A slowdown of the manufacturing sector for the first quarter triggered the downgrade in kw/h sales growth, said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
Sales growth was also stunted because a number of big consumers were generating their own power, Reyes said.

"We came from a high base last year because there were few negative factors unlike the typhoons in 1995. This year, there will be improvement in kw/h sales volume but it will not be exciting," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping & Associates.
In 1996, Meralco's sales rose 12.2 percent to 17.81 billion kw/hs. Operating revenues for the same year were 57.08 billion pesos.
Gene Gabriel, an analyst at Sun Hung Kai, said he expected operating revenues for 1997 to reach 61.55 billion pesos, 7.8 percent higher than 1996.
Meralco president Manuel Lopez earlier said he expected the company to post 9.5 percent growth in sales but did not give a figure in pesos.
Philippine Asia Equity analyst Gina Manzano said that a strike at Manila Paper Mills, a major Meralco customer, also contributed to the gloomy sales picture for the year.
But some analysts said Meralco might yet be redeemed by revenues from its property unit Rockwell Land Corp, in which it has a 70 percent stake.
Rockwell is developing a 15.5 hectare (38.75 acre) site near the Makati business district into a commercial and residential centre.
"The projected loss in energy sales maybe compensated by contributions from Rockwell. They may balance each other out," Manzano said.

However, ING Barings said it did not expect Rockwell revenues to do wonders for Meralco's bottom line. But it saw second-quarter electricity sales growing between seven to eight percent, better than the first quarter's 5.4 percent.

"It's not something within their control. They don't have control of how fast Rockwell can be built," said ING analyst Giovanni de la Rosa, who planned to lower his sales growth forecast to about eight percent from 10 percent.
Despite the downgrade in sales growth, Guoco Securities research head Saturnino Mejia recommended a long-term buy on Meralco.
"It provides a basic service and it remains a core holding among Asian portfolios," he said.
